result.title: Events, Not Pixels: Where World Models Get the Return Wrong
result.summary: World models are increasingly used for planning, where a planner ranks candidate actions by returns imagined by the model. However, these models are judged mainly by how well they render frames, even though a visually faithful rollout can still assign the wrong return. To identify where this mismatch arises, we introduce a transition-level diagnostic that replaces imagined transitions with real ones and measures the reduction in return error against a budget-matched random control. Our analysis yields two findings. (1) Event transitions, the few steps where a reward is earned or an episode ends, are rendered as well as other steps (median pixel-error ratio 0.85), yet restoring them removes a median of 70% of the return error. In contrast, restoring transitions with the largest MSE, SSIM or LPIPS error removes less than a random choice. Across the 44 Atari-100k model--collection pairs that pass our reliability checks, including three released families, event patches outperform random patches in 39 (sign test p=1.4 x 10^{-7}), with a median gain of +44 percentage points. (2) The remaining error is structured: a complementary patch separates errors at true events from those elsewhere, while an eight-step timing tolerance recovers few events missed by our deterministic models. This structure also guides repair: a rule recorded before four repair outcomes were known predicts when a diffusion model repairs these failures. Event patches improve plan ranking, and the same concentration appears on control tasks with rare reward events.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对世界模型用于规划时的 return 预测，提出 transition 级诊断：把想象的 transition 替换为真实的，并对照等预算的随机替换，测量 return 误差的下降幅度；发现事件 transition（获得奖励或回合终止的少数步骤）渲染精度与其他步骤相当，却承载了大部分 return 误差。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「替换真实 transition + budget-matched 随机对照」的干预式归因思路，可能可供核查 LVR 中哪些 latent 状态或视觉证据真正影响答案与停止决策，以及渲染保真度与决策相关正确性之间的错位。
